chief_complaint: Follow-up for hypertension and metabolic risk factor management (obesity, prediabetes) with psychosocial stressors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 42‑year‑old male with longstanding essential hypertension diagnosed in 2013, currently treated with lisinopril and low‑dose amlodipine. Blood pressure is controlled at 110/82 mmHg but requires two agents, suggesting persistent risk. Obesity (BMI ≥30) was documented in 2017 and remains unchanged. Prediabetes was identified in May 2023 (A1c 6.2%). Since 2023 the patient also reports increased social isolation, chronic stress, part‑time employment, and ongoing transportation barriers, all compounded by refugee status. No recent lipid panel, renal function, or BMI measurements are available. Preventive care appears incomplete, and a medication review flag has been active since 2021.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include acute infective cystitis (2023), prior full‑time employment periods, previous episodes of stress (resolved 2022 and 2018), previous part‑time employment (resolved 2021), unemployment resolved 2018, and unhealthy alcohol drinking behavior resolved 2022. No chronic organ‑specific diseases other than those listed as active.
social_determinants: Refugee status, lack of reliable transportation, part‑time employment with limited income, social isolation, chronic stress, and limited access to healthcare resources.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 1 hypertension (SBP 110, DBP 82), elevated resting heart rate (99 bpm), obesity, prediabetes (A1c 6.2%). Metabolic risk: obesity and prediabetes increase likelihood of progression to type 2 diabetes and dyslipidemia (lipid values missing). Renal risk cannot be assessed (eGFR missing). Psychosocial risk: social isolation, stress, refugee background, transportation barriers. Overall clinical complexity is moderate; Charlson comorbidity index is 0.

Renal function (eGFR) not recorded; cannot assess CKD risk.
Lipid panel missing; ASCVD risk calculation incomplete.
Current alcohol consumption not documented; only past unhealthy use resolved.
Medication indications are unspecified in the record.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with multiple interrelated cardiometabolic risk factors—hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes—managed only with antihypertensive therapy. Preventive care gaps (missing lipid, renal, and BMI data) and significant psychosocial determinants (refugee status, transportation barriers, social isolation) increase the likelihood of disease progression and suboptimal adherence. Overall health is stable but requires comprehensive risk assessment, lifestyle intervention, and addressing social barriers.
